findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with === always false
findings.body: The check that a date override marks the whole day unavailable compares two freshly created Dayjs instances with `===`. This is reference equality, so it is never true. Overrides where start equals end (a day marked unavailable) are not caught by this branch. They only behave correctly by accident through the later isBefore/isSame checks. Compare with `.isSame()` or `.valueOf()` instead.

findings.title: Working hours end check uses slot start instead of slot end
findings.body: `end` is computed from `slotStartTime`, the same value as `start`. A slot that begins inside working hours but ends after them passes the check. The intended end-of-slot validation never happens. `end` should be derived from `slotEndTime`.

findings.title: Any single non-matching working-hours entry rejects the slot
findings.body: `workingHours.find` returns true as soon as any entry covering that weekday does not contain the slot. Users commonly have several availability ranges on the same day (e.g. 9-12 and 13-17). A slot at 14:00 falls outside the 9-12 entry, so it is wrongly rejected. The logic should reject a slot only when no working-hours entry contains it (use `some` and negate).

findings.title: Date override day comparison uses incorrectly shifted time
findings.body: `date.start` is already an absolute UTC instant, yet the code adds the negated organizer offset to it before formatting the day. The result is then compared with the UTC slot date. For organizers far from UTC, the shift moves the override onto the wrong UTC calendar day. The start and end bounds are shifted the same way, so slots are wrongly accepted or rejected. Overrides near midnight UTC may never match, or may match the adjacent day.

findings.title: Override minutes wrap across midnight
findings.body: The override start and end are converted to minutes using `hour()*60+minute()` after applying the offset. If the shifted time crosses midnight, the value wraps. A shifted end at 00:30 the next day becomes 30, which is less than the start, and the slot range is silently dropped. Overrides near day boundaries in the invitee timezone are therefore lost.

findings.title: Timezone test doesn't exercise the fixed-host round-robin fix
findings.body: The new test only re-queries a single-user event in another invitee timezone. The headline fix, that date overrides of fixed hosts apply in round-robin events, has no test. The organizer/override timezone mismatch case is also not covered.
